dedupe_keys.name: global inventory of potentially cultivable land and potentially available cropland 1980 2100

description: Global maps of where cropland could expand now and under future climate. The Zenodo record says the dataset gives potentially cultivable land, defined by agricultural suitability for 23 food, feed, fibre and bioenergy crops and the technical feasibility of farming, and potentially available cropland, which also excludes forests, wetlands and strictly protected areas under nature protection policies. Maps cover four periods (1980-2009, 2010-2039, 2040-2069 and 2070-2099) under RCP2.6 and RCP8.5 and consider current irrigation. The data are a free download (a 4.07 GB zip) under CC BY 4.0, published 3 February 2022. Coverage is global. Caveats: suitability rests on modelled climate and does not include economic factors. For simulation it shows how climate change moves the land available for crops, for long-term agricultural exposure and adaptation studies. A related catalogue record is the Zabel natural potential for future cropland expansion.
